rewrites.summary:
Same-sex conduct is criminalised under the national penal code with penalties up to 20 years' imprisonment and caning; legal gender recognition is unavailable, and a dual court system applies Sharia jurisdiction to Muslims only, so same-sex intimacy and 'cross-dressing' are criminalised for Muslims under religious-law enactments. No national law prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, and discrimination and violence against LGBT people are regularly reported, with transgender people particularly vulnerable.

The enforcement pattern a visitor encounters is the national one: a 2022 human-rights report documents state religious authorities harassing LGBT activists and organisations and raiding private events across the parent nation, and the country-profile source records an anti-LGBT crackdown in progress since the 2018 election. The audited sources document no state/province-specific enforcement pattern; the national framework governs what a visitor encounters here.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Parent-nation policy turbulence: the country-profile source records enforcement actions running under the anti-LGBT crackdown in other units of the parent nation — an October 2022 raid on a Queer Halloween party in the capital at which at least 20 LGBT people were arrested, an August raid on an LGBT venue with twenty men arrested, a religious court in another unit ordering a lesbian couple caned, and November 2023 plans for conversion-therapy centres in yet another unit. The human-rights report further records government-run 'rehabilitation' programmes that over a thousand people (at least 1,733) had attended as of June 2021.
rewrites.localsOnly: No Sarawak-specific resident-facing data is recorded in the audited sources: no cultural-role, birth-register practice, resident discrimination statistic or local survey specific to Sarawak appears in the dossier, and the 2022 report's interview base of 73 people across the parent nation yields no documented Sarawak-specific finding.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The audited sources record no Sarawak-specific enforcement case, so the assessment rests on the nationwide framework; absence of a documented local pattern is not proof that none exists.
